title: Align the part to a setup's frame (stock follows), separate from the G54 work offset

labels.name: source:agent
labels.description: Opened by an AI agent (not a human reporter)

body:
Part of the multi-setup chain (#308). No issue in the chain lets the user **orient the part for a setup** so its stock comes out correctly oriented. Today there are only two levers, and both are wrong for this:

- **`MoveModel`** (`crates/app/src/commands/move_model.rs`) places the part rigidly in the *document* - one pose for every setup. Re-orienting it for setup 2 re-orients it for setup 1 too.
- **3-2-1 / "Set WCS orientation from selection"** (#187) rotates the *work offset* (G54...), not the part. Posting a rotated offset is now refused by name (#315, PR #325), so it can't orient a part for machining either.

The stock is an axis-aligned grid in world (`stock_sim.rs`: "The document's stock, as an axis-aligned grid in world"), so a part whose faces aren't square to world gets a stock box that doesn't match how it sits on the machine.

## Two different frames - keep them apart
1. **Setup frame (the setup's "global" / machine-table frame):** how the part sits on the machine for this setup - which face is up, which edge runs along X. The part is placed into this frame by a per-setup rigid transform. **The stock is built axis-aligned in this frame** (box/cylinder/from-model all follow), and toolpaths are generated in it. This is where a 3-2-1 / face-edge-bore pick belongs: "this face is the table, this edge is +X".
2. **Work offset (G54..G59, #196):** where program zero sits on the already-aligned part - normally a pure translation (corner, centre, top of stock, a bore). Rotation on the offset stays the exception (probing compensation), refused for now (#315).

## Proposal
- **Per-setup part alignment:** an undoable `AlignPartToSetup` command (or the `SetSetupTransform` of #316 - one stored transform part -> setup frame, not two) driven by:
  - 3-2-1 picks (primary face -> setup -Z/table, secondary edge/face -> +X, tertiary -> +Y), reusing #187's pick machinery but writing the **part's** transform, not the offset's;
  - presets (face up / flip about X/Y / rotate 90/180/270 about Z);
  - numeric entry.
- **Stock follows:** stock bounds/fit (incl. Fit to Models, #230) are computed in the setup frame from the transformed part; the viewport shows the setup with the part aligned and the stock square to it.
- **Work offset after alignment:** the G54 picker/placement (#196) works on the aligned part (corner/centre/top presets), translation only by default.
- **Posting/verification:** toolpaths, sim and the verifier all run in the setup frame; the posted coordinates are setup-frame minus the offset translation. No rotated offset needed for an aligned part, so #315's refusal no longer bites in normal use.
- Existing documents: identity transform per setup = exactly today's behaviour (implicit-setup law); saved files without the key load identically.

## Relation to the chain
- Shares storage with **#316** (the part -> setup transform *is* this alignment; the transform between two setups is derived from their two alignments). Do this with or before #316; #317-#319 consume it.
- Needs **#196** (offset per setup) for the work-offset half; complements **#315** (refuse rotated offsets) and **#187** (picks).
- Lathe: the fitted spindle axis already defines the turning frame (lathe axis-fit work); this issue is milling/mill-turn setups first.

## Done means
A part can be aligned to a setup by 3-2-1 picks, presets or numbers through an undoable command; the stock (box, cylinder, from model, Fit to Models) is axis-aligned in that setup's frame; generation, sim, verify and post run in the setup frame and post correct coordinates with an unrotated G54 placed on the aligned part; two setups can hold the same part in different orientations without touching each other; identity alignment posts byte-identically to today; pinned by tests for each.
